major_events: In Chapter 1416, Su Ming accepts the Reverse Spirit Bead from Elder Gu Tai, triggering the instantaneous reunification of his four true worlds' wills within his soul.
In Chapter 1416, Gu Tai witnesses the rise of a combined will aura around Su Ming, identifying it as the signature power of a Ninth-Level Dao Deity.
In Chapter 1417, Su Ming projects his first Dao Spirit Sound in the open skies of the Seven Month Sect, formally declaring his participation in the Imperial succession struggle.

In Chapter 1420, Su Ming depletes his physical vitality to sigh the 9th Dao Spirit Sound of Destiny, causing his face to manifest across the skies of the entire Gu Zang country and penetrate the Imperial Capital.
In Chapter 1422, Gu Tai escorts Su Ming to a remote northwestern village where he meets the Nine-fold Dao Deity Gu Hong, who is living in disguise as a simple woodcutter.
In Chapter 1425, when two Dao Deities from Yi Dao Sect launch an assassination attempt, Gu Hong uses his axe to slice their fate-charts, permanently transforming them into white dogs.
In Chapter 1427 and 1428, Xiu Luo Sect's Great Elder Ji Wumeng arrives to capture Su Ming but is caught by Gu Hong, who drains her cultivation and forces her to submit to comical interrogation.
In Chapter 1429, Su Ming declines Gu Hong's offer to directly inherit Ji Wumeng's cultivation, declaring his true name and detailing his origin from the Sang Xiang world.
In Chapter 1430, Su Ming formally kneels and accepts Gu Hong as his second master, receiving a crescent moon seal on his palm.
In Chapter 1431, the Nine-fold Dao Deity Xiu Luo visits the village with his biologically male disciple Han Yu, demonstrating his path of Will Deception.
In Chapter 1433, Su Ming arrives at the cavern in the southwest mountains and bypasses the frozen gate of the Xuan Zang Palace using the cultivation of his five guard dogs and time-reversal.
In Chapter 1434, Su Ming spends 240 years in seclusion refining the missing-corner compass and the Star Whip, successfully transforming the mirror reflection of Xuan Zang back into his own face.
In Chapter 1435, Su Ming rescues the cultivator Xu Hui, who shares the face and name of his deceased lover, by commanding his dogs to execute her pursuers from Luo Yun Sect.
In Chapter 1440, Su Ming participates in the first layer of the Dao Proof Realm, slaughtering Yi Dao Sect's Dao Deities to conquer the altars and advance to the 4-fold Dao Spirit Realm.
In Chapter 1449, Su Ming utilizes the giant Divine Wood from the Sang Xiang world to catapult himself up the central tree, overtaking the other princes to reach the 9th Heaven first.
In Chapter 1453, during the collapse of the third layer of the Dao Proof Realm, the tree spirit Hao Hao recognizes Su Ming's familiar aura and projects him into the original native world.
In Chapter 1465 and 1466, Hao Hao chooses to revert into a seed in the native world's lake, starting a 2,700-year cycle of restoration while Su Ming guards him and reaches the 8-fold Dao尊 level.
In Chapter 1471 and 1473, Su Ming returns to the Gu Zang country, finds the Seven Month Sect devastated, and invades Yi Dao Sect to execute their Great Dao尊s Bai Lu and Chi Yang in blood revenge.
In Chapter 1481, Su Ming ascends the 33 Heavens, enters the brow of the giant black-robed Xuan Zang, and successfully possesses him, waking up as a solitary supreme deity in the real Void.

In the Final Chapter, Su Ming sacrifices his own life force to revive the dead world within his body, collecting the soul fragments of his deceased friends across millions of years so they can live happily on the Ninth Summit.
character_state_transitions: Su Ming transitions from a low-profile cultivator in the Seven Month Sect to a recognized candidate with four active true world wills restored to his soul.
Su Ming transitions from an unstable pre-Dao Spirit level to a fully consolidated silver-auraed Dao Spirit Realm cultivator after projecting the 9th Dao Spirit Sound.
The two Yi Dao Sect Dao Deities transition from proud human assassins to domestic white guard dogs with their cultivation sealed and their fates restructured.
Ji Wumeng transitions from a haughty Xiu Luo Sect Great Elder to a terrified, cultivation-drained petitioner fleeing in embarrassment.
Su Ming transitions from an uncommitted candidate to the formal disciple of Gu Hong, accepting the crescent moon mark on his palm.
Su Ming transitions from a seeker of the Star Whip to its master, successfully refining both the whip and the missing-corner compass after 240 years of seclusion.
The First Prince transitions into a temporary vessel hosting the consciousness and Great Dao尊 power of Lin Dongdong.
Su Ming transitions from a competitor in the Dao Proof Realm to a patient protector of a world's rebirth, spending 2,700 years in isolation and achieving 8-fold Dao尊 cultivation.
Dao Han transitions from a comatose, severely injured state in a frozen coffin to a revived, emotional leader witnessing Su Ming's return as an Great Dao尊.
Su Ming transitions from a dreamlike prince in the Gu Zang memory-world to the supreme, solitary ruler of the Void, experiencing absolute isolation.
The deceased companions of the Ninth Summit transition from shattered soul-fragments in the Void to resurrected entities with their original memories intact in Su Ming's internal world.
long_form_mechanisms: The Dao Spirit Sound (道灵音) functions as a rite of passage where a cultivator projects their voice to merge with the heavens and earth. It scales from 1 (initial) to 9 (extreme). High-level projections cause severe vital backlash but permanently rewrite the candidate's talent, guaranteeing the path to Great Dao尊 status.

Gu Hong's Destiny-Slicing Axe (斩命格) is a metaphysical method that treats targets as wood blocks. By focusing beyond the physical form, the user slices the underlying destiny-chart and memory-runes, causing an irreversible, biological transformation of the target into domestic animals.

The Will Deception Dao (意志欺骗之道) operates on the principle that reality is merely an illusion imposed by supreme wills. If a cultivator is raised in an environment where they are treated under a specific false condition (e.g. gender-bending Han Yu), their physical and spiritual structure conforms to that belief.

The Time-Reversal Bypass (岁月逆转) allows Su Ming to circumvent the entry restrictions of the Xuan Zang Palace. By channeling the combined energy of his dog companions, he reverses the local temporal state of the ice gate to a time prior to its locking, dissolving the barrier without performing the required bows.

Great Dao尊 Consciousness Possession is a method where a supreme master projects their consciousness into a descendant host in the Dao Proof Realm, replacing their soul and granting them temporary Great Dao尊 power at the cost of severe physical damage to the host.

Hao Hao's World Reconstruction Seed mechanism involves the tree spirit planting itself in the native world's central lake. Over 2,700 years, it draws energy from the Void, growing into a million-foot tree whose roots restore oceans, rivers, and green environments to the dead continents.

The Dream-Possession of Xuan Zang (夺舍与梦境显化) dictates that the entire Gu Zang country was the final, dying memory-world of Xuan Zang. By successfully traversing this dream, refining the compass and Star Whip, and stepping into Xuan Zang's brow, Su Ming overwrites Xuan Zang's consciousness to possess his physical body in reality.

World Re-creation and Soul Re-summoning involves Su Ming sacrificing his own life force to sustain his internal world. He disperses Xuan Zang's hand-beads as butterflies to gather the soul-fragments of his friends across cosmic cycles, opening the Underworld Gate to revive them with intact memories.
continuity_observations: The Divine Wood utilized by Su Ming to ascend the central tree is theorized to be a branch of the original Dao Proof Tree that drifted into the Void, linking the ecosystems of the two worlds.
The missing-corner compass found in the Xuan Zang Palace matches the physical compass that Xuan Zang sits on in the real Void, serving as a key object linking the dream-world to reality.
The Star Whip, initially an imperial treasure, takes the form of a black dragon-headed python inside the Xuan Zang Palace before shrinking into a simple black thread wristlet on Su Ming's wrist.
The crescent moon mark given to Su Ming by Gu Hong in the village is later employed by Su Ming to absorb and deflect the high-level attack of Lin Dongdong during the tree ascent.
The white guard dogs transformed from the enemy Dao Deities remain as persistent companions, providing both comedic relief and critical cultivation support for Su Ming's time-reversal spell.
The 2,700 years Su Ming spends in the native world with Hao Hao runs parallel to the time flow in the Gu Zang country, showing a 1:1 temporal synchronization between the two dimensions.

The cultivator Xu Hui whom Su Ming rescues in the mountains shares the face and name of his deceased lover, representing a localized reincarnation of her soul-fragments within the Gu Zang memory-world.
The six butterflies that house the worlds of the previous novels are revealed to be transformed from six of the seven hand-beads of Xuan Zang, which Su Ming disperses into the Void.
style_observations: The text heavily utilizes philosophical dialogues on truth, illusion, and subjective reality (真假之争) to frame the protagonist's growth and the nature of the universe.
The author employs a melancholic, elegiac tone filled with descriptions of drifting snow, gray horizons, and lonely figures to emphasize the theme of solitude.
Combat is structured around precise calculations (精算) and tactical manipulation of environmental rules rather than simple clashes of energy.
The ending establishes clear crossover connections with the author's other works (Xian Ni and Wo Yu Feng Tian) through the character of Mie Sheng and the search for the crane.
High-stakes drama is frequently subverted by comical, absurd scenarios, such as a supreme Nine-fold Dao Deity acting as a lecherous, wood-chopping villager.
The narrative uses repetitive poetic refrains (e.g. '几多轮回少一人') to reinforce the central themes of memory, persistence, and tragic sacrifice.

creation_family_evidence.author: Er Gen (耳根)
shared_universe_indicators: Appearance of Wang Lin and Li Muwan from Xian罡 (Xian Ni) in the Postscript
Mie Sheng's departure to search for the bald crane, directly setting up the events of Wo Yu Feng Tian
recurring_motifs: Ninth Summit (第九峰) as the ultimate home
The Underworld Gate (冥门) for soul resurrection
Dao Wu Ya (道无涯) as the peak of cultivation
Time Reversal (岁月逆转) as a core technique
creation_family_evidence.thematic_signature: The representation of '魔' (devil/demon) as an uncompromising obsession to protect one's memories and past companions against the indifference of the cosmos.

originality_risks: The heavy reliance on crossovers and characters from other novels (such as Wang Lin and the bald crane) in the postscript makes the ending dependent on external works.
The 'all a dream/memory' trope (庄周梦蝶) used for the Gu Zang country risks trivializing the development, relationships, and battles of the preceding arc.
The motif of self-sacrifice where the protagonist remains dead/alone while his resurrected friends live happily is a recurring xianxia trope that may feel repetitive.
The character Han Yu being raised as a female solely to prove a philosophical point about deception risks being perceived as biologically reductive or insensitive.
